name: Hookline Independent Freight Night Haul Kit
description:
The working uniform of an independent dock and freight hauler running night shifts on the Circuit-level cargo corridors — no corponation logo, no issued kit, everything sourced personally and maintained obsessively. The base is a heavyweight dark navy cargo trouser from Goretek — HaulMaster cut, with reinforced inner thighs, six pockets including two deep side-cargo pockets with compression buckles, and a wide belt loop arrangement that accommodates a tool-and-tether harness. The trouser legs are slightly flared at the ankle to accommodate a digitigrade leg prosthetic on the left side, the seam there hand-opened and restitched with orange industrial thread — a visible repair that's also a practical modification. On top: a Sable Freight thermal henley in dark brown, long-sleeved, with a kangaroo chest pocket that holds a flex-screen work manifest. Over it, a high-vis orange safety vest — generic market-bought, no branding — with reflective silver strips at chest and hem, multiple D-ring attachment points, and a built-in radio holster on the left chest.

Boots are Dockmaster Deepwade — waterproof, steel-toe, ankle-height with a side-zip for fast removal. A wide-brimmed matte-black rain hat with a synth-wax finish and a hi-vis orange band around the crown keeps acid-drizzle off the neck. Thick fingerless work gloves in gray synth-leather leave the fingertips free for manifest-screen operation. A battered personal light — magnetic clip-mount, warm amber beam — clips to the vest's shoulder strap. The whole kit is dark, functional, and anonymous: no name patch, no affiliation. Just the work.
functionality: Six-pocket cargo trousers with compression buckles, hand-modified flared leg seam for digitigrade prosthetic, radio holster vest, D-ring tether attachment points, waterproof steel-toe boots, flex-screen manifest pocket, magnetic clip light, acid-rain-resistant hat brim
what_it_says: Independent. Not corponation-employed — which means no benefits, no union card, but also no one monitoring your manifest times or scanning your cargo too closely. The hand-modified trouser leg is the first thing anyone notices: whoever this is, they have a prosthetic limb and they did the alteration themselves, which means they're resourceful and not particularly interested in being pitied. The lack of any branding is a statement: this person works for themselves and trusts no logo.
manufacturer: Goretek (trousers); Sable Freight (henley); Dockmaster (boots); generic circuit market (vest, hat, gloves); self-modified
story_hooks: The flex-screen manifest in the chest pocket contains a hidden partition with a cargo log that contradicts official dock records — someone is systematically skimming containers, and this hauler either knows or is being set up to take the fall.

The hand-modified trouser seam conceals a shallow sewn channel running up the inner leg — it's been used to carry something small and rigid, and whatever it was, it's gone now, but there's dried blood in the seam.
A player character needs a night-shift cargo hauler who won't ask questions about a particular shipment; this kit is the visual signal that its wearer is the right kind of independent — for a price.
